questions.stem: During ventricular systole, what happens to the atrioventricular (AV) valves?

options.text: They open to allow blood into the ventricles
They remain open throughout the cycle
They close to prevent blood flowing back into the atria
They close to prevent blood entering the arteries

questions.explanation: During ventricular systole, the ventricles contract and pressure rises, causing the AV valves to close. This prevents blood from flowing back into the atria and produces the 'lub' sound.
